extracted.intended_audience: Organizations and their representatives participating in the UN Global Compact (e.g., company CSR/comms teams, business associations, compliance officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural expectations for UN Global Compact participants about public communications, required documentation (Letter of Commitment, Communication on Engagement/Progress), publication dates, and removal/redaction policies. Focused on maintaining transparent public records for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of Commitment (appears as a required document when joining the UN Global Compact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of commitment submitted by participants form part of the public record and, per the site's policy, are not deleted even if a participant leaves. The profile lists that a Letter of Commitment exists (e.g., shows 'Participant Since 17 April 2018').

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication on Engagement (COE) — submission and due date
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must provide a Communication on Engagement; the profile shows COE items and a 'Next Communication on Engagement (COE) due on' date (e.g., 19 January 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COEs are published on the participant profile with publication dates and titles. Participants are responsible for ensuring their COE is submitted/published by the stated due date; the profile lists past COEs and their publication dates (examples: 'COE Aberje Brasil (2023-2024)' published 19-Jan-2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication on Progress (CoP) — levels/status note
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on levels: 'Not applicable refers to the period when the Communication on Progress (CoP) did not require differentiation levels.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting with the 2022 Early Adopter Programme, there will no longer be any differentiation levels for the CoP. Users should not assume historical 'levels' apply post-2022 and should follow the Early Adopter Programme's updated labeling/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for content of public communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for the content of participants' public communication related to the Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact and their implementation lies with participants themselves and not with the UN Global Compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are accountable for accuracy and appropriateness of what they publish on their profile (COEs/CoPs). The UN Global Compact disclaims responsibility for participant-published content, making organizational review and compliance necessary before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction and removal policy for CoPs/documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The UN Global Compact can redact personal information but does not delete participant profiles, letters of commitment, or other voluntarily submitted documents (including CoPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may request redaction of names, signatures, and other personal information from your CoP. However, in alignment with standard procedure, complete deletion of the online profile or submitted documents is not performed; see the 'CoP Removal Request Policy' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency and disclosure are core values to which participants adhere when joining the UN Global Compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public database is maintained to ensure a transparent record of current and past participants. Participants should expect that submitted documents and basic profile information remain publicly accessible to uphold transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participant metadata and status fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Profiles display key metadata fields: Type (e.g., Business Association), Country, Global Compact Status (e.g., Active), Participant Since, and links to the organization's website and social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining accurate metadata supports transparency and helps track compliance timelines (e.g., next COE due date). The profile's status and dates are part of the public record and inform stakeholders about a participant's engagement level.
